fix(opencode): re-probe a v1 runtime when the provider is refreshed

### Linked issue

Closes #9583

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Enhancement
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs

### Reasoning

If OpenCode is updated from 1.x to 2.x while the daemon runs, the daemon stays on the v1 client. `OpenCodeRuntimeClient` caches a successful 1.x `--version` probe for the client's lifetime, and a binary update doesn't change provider config, so the client is never rebuilt. Once the old v1 server exits, every OpenCode request fails with `Request is not supported by this version of OpenCode Server (Server responded with text/html)`. The version error message tells users to "Update OpenCode …, then refresh the provider in Paseo", but Refresh and agent Reload both keep failing. Only a daemon restart recovers, and a restart interrupts every running agent.

With this change, a forced provider refresh drops a cached v1 selection and re-probes the binary, so Refresh does what the message says.

### Goals

- A forced catalog refresh (the provider Refresh button / `refresh_providers_snapshot_request`) re-probes a cached v1 selection. New agents then run on v2 without a daemon restart.
- After that refresh, reloading an agent created before the update resumes it on v2 with its conversation intact.
- A cached v2 selection stays as it is: no re-probe and no new client, because it owns live sessions.
- Overlapping forced refreshes probe once, so no duplicate v2 client is created.

### Non-goals

- Agents created before the update are not migrated automatically. They keep their v1 session until they are reloaded, as the QA below shows (S7 → S8).
- No periodic re-probing. A non-forced catalog read still uses the cached selection.
- Downgrades from 2.x to 1.x are not handled.

### QA

Everything below ran on this branch (`8e61f644b`, rebased on `af6ca46ae`) and on unmodified `main` (`af6ca46ae`). Each build had its own isolated dev daemon on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04).

**Setup.**
- Real OpenCode binaries: 1.19.5 (`opencode-ai`) and 2.2.7 (`@opencode/cli`).
- `agents.providers.opencode.command` points at a symlink that I re-point from 1.19.5 to 2.2.7 mid-run.
- The model is a deterministic OpenAI-compatible stub, because my local model host was offline during the final run.
  - It answers "Reply with just the word X" with X.
  - It answers "What is the secret word?" with a word it finds in the conversation history it receives. That makes S9 prove the old agent's history survived the switch to v2.
- I also ran the same matrix on an earlier base (`9e607a3aa`) with a real local Qwen model, and the results matched.

#### Daemon / RPC matrix

One script ran every step on both builds. "servers" is the daemon's child processes in v1 mode (`serve --port N`) and v2 mode (`serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 0`) after each step.

| # | Step | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Create agent on 1.19.5 ("the secret word is APPLE") | OK; v1=1 | OK; v1=1 |
| S2 | Re-point binary to 2.2.7, v1 server exits | v1=0 | v1=0 |
| S3 | Message old agent | ❌ `server.connected event; your message was not sent` | ❌ same |
| S4 | New agent | ❌ `Failed to create OpenCode session: {}` | ❌ same |
| S5 | Forced provider refresh | acknowledged; v1=1 **v2=0** | acknowledged; **v2=1** |
| S6 | New agent after refresh | ❌ `Request is not supported … (text/html)` | ✅ answers `S6` |
| S7 | Message old agent, no reload | ❌ `server.connected event` | ❌ same (still holds its v1 session) |
| S8 | `paseo agent reload` old agent | ❌ `agent_refresh_failed` (text/html) | ✅ reloaded; v1=0 v2=1 |
| S9 | Ask old agent for the secret word | ❌ text/html | ✅ `APPLE` |
| | v1 server generations / text/html log lines | 7 / 8 | 3 / 0 |

#### App (Expo web on the same dev daemons, headless Chromium)

Steps: New workspace → OpenCode model → send (U1) → model selector → OpenCode settings → **Refresh** (U2) → send again (U3).

| Step | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| U1 send before refresh | "Failed to create OpenCode session: {}" | same |
| U2 Refresh | "Request is not supported by this version of OpenCode Server (Server responded with text/html)", no models | Discovered 13 models, "Updated just now" |
| U3 send after refresh | no model can be picked (provider shows Error + Retry) | agent answers; timeline shows "This chat uses OpenCode v2." |

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| After Refresh | ![main after refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkfka1/paseo/qa-9583/qa/9583/base-U2-provider-refresh.png) | ![PR after refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkfka1/paseo/qa-9583/qa/9583/fixed-U2-provider-refresh.png) |
| Send after Refresh | ![main send after refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkfka1/paseo/qa-9583/qa/9583/base-U3-send-after-refresh.png) | ![PR send after refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkfka1/paseo/qa-9583/qa/9583/fixed-U3-send-after-refresh.png) |

#### Tests

Three new tests in `runtime-client.test.ts` (10 cases):
- "re-probes a v1 runtime on a forced refresh after OpenCode is updated to v2"
- "keeps a v2 runtime on a forced refresh without probing the binary again". It counts `--version` invocations.
- "probes once when a second forced refresh starts N microtasks after the first", for N = 0–8. With the `this.selected === current` guard removed, N = 1 probes again and builds a duplicate v2 client.

Results:
- `main` source with the new tests: 9 failed, 22 passed. The v2 case passes on `main` because `main` never re-probes.
- This branch: `npx vitest run src/server/agent/providers/opencode/` → 23 files, 235 tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck` (all workspaces), `npm run lint` and the format check pass. The lefthook pre-commit ran all three.

Platforms: Linux only, using the web app against a dev daemon. The change is daemon-side and platform-independent. I did not test macOS, Windows, or the mobile and desktop apps.

### Checklist

- [ ] Plugin changes follow the [SDK import boundaries](../docs/plugins.md#sdk-import-boundaries) (if applicable)
- [x] One focused change
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run format` passes
- [x] QA evidence
- [x] Tests added or updated where it made sense
